title: upgrade attn: flashattnv2 + fused ops + rope/rotary + kv-batching + scheduler tweaks
description:
Motivation:
We see steady CPU/GPU utilization spikes and suboptimal throughput for mid-length contexts (1k-4k) on recent DDS workloads. This PR upgrades our attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 variants, adds fused rotary/rope code paths, and introduces a scheduling heuristic that prioritizes KV-batched streams to improve throughput and reduce tail latency.

What changed:
- Upgrade FlashAttention submodule to v2.3.1 and adapt runtime kernel API
- Implement fused rotary/rope operator that avoids separate elementwise ops in the attention fastpath
- Add KV-cache-aware batching scheduler: groups inflight requests by compatible KV cache shape and sequence family to increase effective batch size without violating latency SLOs
- Add fallback paths for older GPUs and for models with unsupported rotary formats
- Add microbenchmarks (runtime/benchmarks/attention) and per-kernel telemetry to help triage perf regressions

Checklist:
- [x] Benchmarks: local microbenchmarks (+12-35% throughput on A100 for 2k context)
- [x] Unit tests updated and passing
- [x] E2E smoke on dedicated staging cluster
- [x] Rollout plan: staged canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic revert on increased error rate or latency regression

Compatibility/Notes:
- The fused rotary/rope path is guarded behind a capability flag; default preserves existing behavior for models that rely on legacy rope encoding. Customers can opt into the new path via runtime config.
- This PR touches low-level CUDA kernels; please review the kernel boundary conditions carefully (padding, seq-len remainder handling).

Benchmarks (summary):
- A100, batch35, seq_len=2048: +28% median throughput, tail latency -18%
- T4, batch16, seq_len=1024: +12% throughput (fallback to slower kernel for quantized models)
- KV-batching increase: effective GPU compute utilization up by ~14% in DPS replay tests

Related Linear items: ENG-4123, ENG-4202.

Risks & Rollback:
- Risk: kernel-level memory corruption - mitigated by extensive unit tests and ASAN builds in CI.
- Rollback: can flip capability flag and revert submodule bump; rollback instructions added to runbook (docs/oncall/runbooks/attention-kernel-rollback.md)
